segments.intent: Summarize average body measurements by penguin species
segments.value:
```sql
SELECT
  species,
  COUNT(*) AS penguin_count,
  AVG(bill_length_mm) AS avg_bill_length_mm,
  AVG(bill_depth_mm) AS avg_bill_depth_mm,
  AVG(flipper_length_mm) AS avg_flipper_length_mm,
  AVG(body_mass_g) AS avg_body_mass_g
FROM penguins
GROUP BY species
ORDER BY species
```

<details open><summary>Result</summary>

```
    species penguin_count avg_bill_length_mm avg_bill_depth_mm
1    Adelie           152           38.79139          18.34636
2 Chinstrap            68           48.83382          18.42059
3    Gentoo           124           47.50488          14.98211
  avg_flipper_length_mm avg_body_mass_g
1              189.9536        3700.662
2              195.8235        3733.088
3              217.1870        5076.016
```

</details>

segments.content:
Here are the main species-level differences in average body measurements: | Species | Count | Avg bill length (mm) | Avg bill depth (mm) | Avg flipper length (mm) | Avg body mass (g) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Adelie | 152 | 38.8 | 18.3 | 190.0 | 3700.7 | | Chinstrap | 68 | 48.8 | 18.4 | 195.8 | 3733.1 | | Gentoo | 124 | 47.5 | 15.0 | 217.2 | 5076.0 | Key differences: - **Adelie** are the **smallest overall** by this summary: - shortest bills - shortest flippers - lowest body mass - **Chinstrap** have the **longest bills** and the **deepest bills** on average, but body mass is close to Adelie. - **Gentoo** stand out the most: - **much longer flippers** - **much heavier body mass** - **shallower bills** than the other two species In short: - **Bill shape** separates species well: Chinstrap have longer/deeper bills, Gentoo have long but relatively shallow bills, Adelie have shorter bills. - **Body size** separates Gentoo strongly from the others: they are substantially heavier with longer flippers. These are averages, so there may still be overlap between species in individual birds.
